subject: Step 2: in-Renode-memory single-instruction mutants (no ELF modified)
mechanism: mutrun.sh builds run_mut.resc = run.resc + an injected 'sysbus WriteWord <itcm_addr> <halfword>' after LoadELF, patching ONE instruction of our reconstructed C body (v=1) in emulator memory. Shares the real loaded stock globals. No ELF/image on disk is modified or copied (as ramlayout does).

cheapa (codec_allocate).finding: ERROR branch (mutex-acquire fail -> g2_file_heap_error_log + g2_file_close_error) is UNREACHABLE under current fuzzing. audio_file_mutex_acquire is stubbed K_RET (always returns 0=success), so the normal branch (g2_file_pool_allocate) is always taken.
cheapa (codec_allocate).why_it_matters: this is exactly why the old wrong g2_file_heap_error_log defsym survived as a false EQUAL (step 1).
cheapa (codec_allocate).to_reach_equivalently: patch the SHARED mutex_acquire entry 0x4497b6 in Renode memory to a seeded non-zero return so BOTH v=0 and v=1 take the error branch for some inputs (a paired in-memory override); then the error-branch code is exercised equivalently and a mutant there would be caught. Not yet implemented.
